name: Barbell Bench Press
preparation: Lie flat on the bench with eyes under the bar, feet planted firmly on the floor. Grip the bar just wider than shoulder-width and unrack it over your shoulders.
execution: Lower the bar with control to mid-chest, keeping elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. Press it back up in a straight line until your arms are fully extended.
formTips: Keep your shoulder blades pinched together and your feet driving into the floor for a stable base.
Don't let the bar bounce off your chest — control the descent.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest to generate momentum.
Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees, which stresses the shoulders.
Lifting the hips off the bench to move more weight.
safetyNotes: Always use a spotter or safety bars when pressing near your max -- a failed heavy rep with no bailout is a real risk with this exercise.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
preparation: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, palms facing forward, elbows bent.
execution: Press both dumbbells up and slightly inward until your arms are extended, then lower them back to chest height under control.
formTips: Dumbbells allow a deeper stretch than a barbell — don't drop your elbows below shoulder height if you feel any strain.
Keep the dumbbells moving in sync to avoid tipping.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
preparation: Set a bench to a 30-45 degree incline. Unrack the bar with a grip just wider than shoulder-width.
execution: Lower the bar to your upper chest, then press it back up in a straight line, emphasizing the upper chest and front shoulders.
formTips: A steeper incline shifts more work to the shoulders — 30-45 degrees keeps the emphasis on the upper chest.
Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows at the bottom.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
preparation: On an inclined bench, bring two dumbbells to shoulder level with palms facing forward.
execution: Press the dumbbells up and slightly inward until arms are extended, then lower with control back to shoulder level.
formTips: Avoid flaring your elbows out to 90 degrees — a slight tuck protects your shoulders.
Pause briefly at the top to avoid using momentum.

name: Push-Up
preparation: Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width on the floor, body in a straight line from head to heels.
execution: Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, then push back up to the starting position.
formTips: Keep your core braced so your hips don't sag or pike.
If it's too hard, drop to your knees rather than sacrificing form.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike instead of keeping a straight body line.
Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees instead of a moderate tuck.

name: Chest Dip
preparation: Support yourself on parallel bars with arms extended, and lean your torso slightly forward.
execution: Lower yourself until your shoulders drop just below your elbows, then press back up to full extension.
formTips: Leaning forward shifts the emphasis onto the chest rather than the triceps.
Avoid going too deep if you feel shoulder discomfort.

name: Cable Chest Fly
preparation: Set both pulleys to chest height and step forward with a slight forward lean, one foot ahead of the other.
execution: Sweep the handles in a wide arc until they meet in front of your chest, keeping a slight bend in the elbows, then return under control.
formTips: Focus on squeezing your chest at the point where the handles meet.
Keep the motion smooth — don't let the weight stack slam on the return.

name: Dumbbell Fly
preparation: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand directly above your chest, palms facing each other.
execution: Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc with a slight elbow bend, then bring them back together over your chest.
formTips: Keep the elbow bend constant throughout — don't turn it into a press.
Use a lighter weight than you'd press; this is a stretch-focused movement.

name: Machine Chest Press
preparation: Adjust the seat height so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
execution: Press the handles forward until your arms are extended, then return to the start under control.
formTips: A fixed path makes this a good option for beginners still building pressing technique.
Don't lock your elbows out hard at the top.

name: Pec Deck Machine Fly
preparation: Sit with your back flat against the pad and forearms resting on the levers or handles.
execution: Bring your arms together in front of your chest, squeeze, then return slowly to the starting position.
formTips: Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout to protect the joint.
Control the negative rather than letting the pads snap back.

name: Barbell Deadlift
preparation: Stand with the bar over mid-foot, feet hip-width apart. Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your shins.
execution: Drive through your heels to stand up tall, keeping the bar close to your body and your back flat throughout the pull.
formTips: Brace your core hard before you pull, like you're about to be punched in the stomach.
Keep the bar in contact with your legs the whole way up to avoid it drifting forward.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach the bar instead of hinging with a flat back.
Letting the bar drift away from the shins/thighs during the pull.
Hyperextending the lower back at lockout.
safetyNotes: Keep the bar in contact with your legs throughout -- a bar that drifts forward dramatically increases lower-back stress.
Stop and reset your setup if you lose a flat back partway through the pull rather than grinding through it.

name: Pull-Up
preparation: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width, arms fully extended.
execution: Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, leading with your chest, then lower back down with control.
formTips: Avoid kipping or swinging — a controlled pull builds more back strength.
If you can't do a full rep yet, use an assisted machine or resistance band.
commonMistakes: Using momentum/kipping instead of a controlled pull.
Not achieving a full range of motion (partial reps from a bent-arm start).
safetyNotes: Lower yourself under control on every rep -- dropping suddenly from the top stresses the shoulders and elbows.

name: Lat Pulldown
preparation: Sit with your thighs secured under the pad, and grip the bar wider than shoulder-width.
execution: Pull the bar down to your upper chest while keeping your torso upright, then let it rise back under control.
formTips: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Avoid leaning back excessively to cheat the weight down.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
preparation: Hinge forward at the hips to roughly a 45-degree torso angle with a flat back, holding the bar with an overhand grip.
execution: Pull the bar toward your lower ribs while keeping your elbows close to your body, then lower with control.
formTips: Keep your core braced to protect your lower back throughout the set.
Avoid jerking the weight up with your hips.
commonMistakes: Standing too upright, which turns the row into a shrug instead of a back exercise.
Using momentum from the hips ("body English") instead of pulling with the back.
safetyNotes: Keep your core braced and back flat throughout -- this is a common spot for lower-back strain when fatigued.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
preparation: Place one knee and hand on a bench for support, with the other foot planted on the floor.
execution: Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip with the free arm, squeezing your shoulder blade, then lower under control.
formTips: Keep your torso roughly parallel to the floor and avoid rotating as you pull.
Let the shoulder blade protract fully at the bottom for a full range of motion.

name: Seated Cable Row
preparation: Sit with knees slightly bent and feet braced on the platform, holding the handle with arms extended.
execution: Pull the handle toward your torso while keeping your back straight, squeeze your shoulder blades together, then extend back out.
formTips: Avoid rounding your lower back as you reach forward.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you pull.

name: T-Bar Row
preparation: Straddle the bar with a hinged torso and flat back, gripping the handles.
execution: Pull the handles up toward your chest, keeping elbows close to your body, then lower under control.
formTips: Keep your neck neutral — don't crane your head up to see the weight.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of each rep.

name: Chin-Up
preparation: Hang from a bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip, arms fully extended.
execution: Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar, then lower with control back to a full hang.
formTips: The underhand grip recruits more biceps than a standard pull-up.
Avoid stopping short at the top — a full chin-over-bar rep counts most.
commonMistakes: Using momentum/kipping instead of a controlled pull.
Not achieving a full range of motion (partial reps from a bent-arm start).
safetyNotes: Lower yourself under control on every rep -- dropping suddenly from the top stresses the shoulders and elbows.

name: Face Pull
preparation: Set the pulley to roughly face height and grip the rope with both hands, palms facing in.
execution: Pull the rope toward your face while flaring your elbows out wide, squeezing your rear shoulders and upper back.
formTips: Aim to finish with your hands beside your ears, not your chin.
Use a light weight — this is a technique-focused movement for shoulder health.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
preparation: Stand facing a high pulley, gripping the bar with arms extended almost straight in front of you.
execution: Pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs, keeping a slight elbow bend, then let it rise back under control.
formTips: Keep the movement isolated to your shoulder joint — don't bend your elbows more as you pull.
Slight forward lean helps you feel the lats working.

name: Overhead Barbell Press
preparation: Stand with the bar racked at shoulder height, feet hip-width apart, core braced.
execution: Press the bar straight overhead until your arms lock out, then lower it back to shoulder height under control.
formTips: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core to avoid arching your lower back.
Move your head slightly back and then through as the bar passes your face.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back excessively to help the bar past the face.
Pressing the bar forward instead of straight up, which wastes leverage.
safetyNotes: Brace your core throughout to protect your lower back from the arch this lift tends to encourage.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
preparation: Seated or standing, bring two dumbbells up to shoulder height with palms facing forward.
execution: Press the dumbbells straight overhead until your arms extend, then lower them back with control.
formTips: Avoid arching your lower back to gain height — keep your ribs down.
Don't let the dumbbells drift forward of your shoulders.

name: Arnold Press
preparation: Start with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your shoulders, palms facing you.
execution: As you press overhead, rotate your palms to face forward, reversing the rotation as you lower back down.
formTips: The rotation adds extra work through the full range of the shoulder — keep it slow and controlled.
Use a lighter weight than a standard press until the rotation feels natural.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
preparation: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, with a slight bend in the elbows.
execution: Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until arms are roughly parallel to the floor, then lower with control.
formTips: Lead with your elbows rather than your hands.
Avoid using momentum by swinging the weights up.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
preparation: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
execution: Raise the dumbbells straight out in front of you to shoulder height, keeping a slight elbow bend, then lower with control.
formTips: Avoid swinging your torso to generate momentum.
You can alternate arms if lifting both at once feels too heavy.

name: Rear Delt Fly
preparation: Hinge forward at the hips holding a dumbbell in each hand, with a slight bend in the elbows.
execution: Raise the dumbbells out to the sides, squeezing your rear shoulders at the top, then lower with control.
formTips: Keep your torso still — the movement should come from your shoulders, not your back swinging.
Use a light weight; this is a small, isolation-focused muscle group.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
preparation: Stand side-on to a low pulley, gripping the handle with your outside hand.
execution: Raise the handle out and up to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend, then lower under control.
formTips: The cable keeps tension on the shoulder throughout, unlike a dumbbell at the bottom of the rep.
Keep your torso upright rather than leaning away from the machine.

name: Upright Row
preparation: Stand holding a barbell or dumbbells in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
execution: Pull the weight straight up along your body toward chin height, leading with your elbows, then lower with control.
formTips: Stop if you feel shoulder pinching — a wider grip can help reduce impingement.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout the pull.
commonMistakes: Pulling the bar too high (above chest height), which increases shoulder impingement risk.
safetyNotes: Stop if you feel any shoulder pinching -- a wider grip or lower pull height usually resolves it.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
preparation: Adjust the seat so the handles start at shoulder height.
execution: Press straight up until your arms extend, then lower back under control.
formTips: A fixed path is a good option if you're still building overhead pressing strength.
Don't shrug your shoulders up as you press.

name: Resistance Band Pull-Apart
preparation: Hold a resistance band with both hands at shoulder width, arms extended in front of you.
execution: Pull the band apart by squeezing your shoulder blades together until it touches your chest, then return with control.
formTips: Great as a warm-up for pressing days to activate the rear shoulders.
Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.

name: Barbell Back Squat
preparation: Position the bar across your upper back (not your neck), feet shoulder-width apart, and unrack it.
execution: Bend at the hips and knees to lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive back up through your heels.
formTips: Keep your knees tracking over your toes rather than caving inward.
Brace your core before descending, like you're about to take a punch.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward as the weight gets heavier.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the rep instead of keeping a neutral spine.
Rising with the hips first, turning the squat into a good-morning.
safetyNotes: Use safety bars or pins set just below your bottom position when squatting heavy without a spotter.
Stop the descent if you can't maintain a neutral lower back -- depth isn't worth a rounded spine.

name: Front Squat
preparation: Rest the bar across your front shoulders with elbows raised high, fingertips lightly supporting the bar.
execution: Squat down while keeping your torso upright, then drive back up through your heels.
formTips: An upright torso is essential — leaning forward will roll the bar off your shoulders.
This variation shifts more emphasis onto the quads and core than a back squat.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows drop, which lets the bar roll forward off the shoulders.
Leaning the torso forward instead of staying upright.
safetyNotes: Be ready to bail forward (dump the bar) or use a squat rack with pins -- front squats are harder to bail backward from.

name: Leg Press
preparation: Sit in the machine with feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
execution: Lower the platform until your knees reach about 90 degrees, then press back up without locking your knees out hard.
formTips: Don't let your lower back round off the seat pad at the bottom of the movement.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your feet.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back round off the seat pad at the bottom of the movement.
Locking the knees out hard at the top of every rep.
safetyNotes: Never fully lock and hold your knees under heavy load -- keep a slight bend to avoid transferring stress to the joint.

name: Romanian Deadlift
preparation: Stand holding the bar at hip height with a slight bend in your knees.
execution: Hinge at the hips and lower the bar down the front of your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand.
formTips: Keep the bar close to your legs the entire time.
This is a hip-hinge, not a squat — your knee bend should stay roughly constant.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees too much, turning it into a conventional deadlift instead of a hip hinge.
Rounding the back to reach further down than your hamstring flexibility allows.
safetyNotes: Stop the descent at the point your lower back would round -- range of motion varies a lot by hamstring flexibility.

name: Walking Lunge
preparation: Stand tall, optionally holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
execution: Step forward into a lunge until both knees reach about 90 degrees, then push off your front foot to step into the next lunge.
formTips: Keep your torso upright rather than leaning forward over your front leg.
Take a long enough step that your front knee doesn't travel past your toes.
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee travel far past the toes on a short step.
Leaning the torso forward instead of staying upright.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
preparation: Rest one foot behind you on a bench, standing far enough forward that your front shin stays roughly vertical.
execution: Lower your back knee toward the floor, then drive up through your front heel.
formTips: Most of the work should be through your front leg — the back foot is just for balance.
Start with bodyweight only until your balance feels solid.

name: Leg Extension
preparation: Sit with your shins behind the pad and back flat against the seat.
execution: Extend your legs until straight, squeeze your quads at the top, then lower back under control.
formTips: Avoid locking your knees out violently — control the top of the rep.
Slow the lowering phase down to increase the muscle-building stimulus.

name: Leg Curl
preparation: Lie face down (or sit, depending on the machine) with the pad positioned behind your ankles.
execution: Curl your heels toward your glutes, then lower back under control.
formTips: Avoid lifting your hips off the pad to cheat the weight up.
A brief pause at full contraction improves hamstring engagement.

name: Goblet Squat
preparation: Hold a kettlebell or dumbbell close to your chest with both hands.
execution: Squat down between your knees while keeping your torso upright, then stand back up.
formTips: A great squat pattern to learn before progressing to a barbell squat.
Keep your elbows inside your knees at the bottom of the movement.
commonMistakes: Letting the heels lift off the floor as you descend.
Leaning too far forward instead of keeping the chest up.

name: Standing Calf Raise
preparation: Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised platform or step, heels hanging off the edge.
execution: Rise up onto the balls of your feet as high as possible, pause, then lower your heels below the platform for a full stretch.
formTips: Full range of motion matters more than heavy weight for calf development.
Pause briefly at the top for a stronger contraction.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
preparation: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a padded barbell across your hips.
execution: Drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees, then lower with control.
formTips: Tuck your chin slightly and avoid overextending your lower back at the top.
Drive through your heels, not your toes.
commonMistakes: Overextending the lower back at the top instead of stopping at a straight hip line.
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels.
safetyNotes: Use a pad on the bar -- the unpadded bar directly across the hips is uncomfortable and can bruise without one.

name: Kettlebell Swing
preparation: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell on the floor a short distance in front of you.
execution: Hinge at the hips to swing the kettlebell back between your legs, then snap your hips forward to drive it up to chest height.
formTips: The power comes from your hips, not your arms — think of it as an explosive hip hinge.
Keep your back flat throughout; don't round over as you hinge.
commonMistakes: Squatting the weight up instead of driving it with a hip hinge.
Using the arms to lift the kettlebell instead of letting hip drive do the work.
safetyNotes: Keep your back flat throughout the hinge -- this is a ballistic movement and a rounded back under momentum is riskier than under a slow lift.

name: Barbell Bicep Curl
preparation: Stand holding the bar with a shoulder-width, underhand grip, arms extended.
execution: Curl the bar up toward your shoulders keeping your elbows fixed at your sides, then lower with control.
formTips: Avoid swinging your hips to generate momentum.
Keep your wrists straight rather than curling them at the top.
commonMistakes: Swinging the hips/torso to help lift the weight.
Only completing the top half of the range of motion.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
preparation: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
execution: Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders, keeping elbows pinned at your sides, then lower under control.
formTips: Alternate arms if it helps you keep strict form.
Avoid letting your elbows drift forward as the weight gets heavy.

name: Hammer Curl
preparation: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing your body.
execution: Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders, then lower with control.
formTips: The neutral grip targets the brachialis and forearms in addition to the biceps.
Keep your upper arms still throughout the movement.

name: Cable Bicep Curl
preparation: Stand facing a low pulley, gripping a straight or EZ bar attachment with an underhand grip.
execution: Curl the handle up toward your shoulders keeping your elbows fixed, then lower under control.
formTips: The cable keeps constant tension on the biceps, unlike a dumbbell at the bottom of the rep.
Stand far enough back that the cable stays taut throughout.

name: Concentration Curl
preparation: Sit on a bench, brace the back of your upper arm against your inner thigh, and let the dumbbell hang.
execution: Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, focusing on a strict, isolated motion, then lower with control.
formTips: This variation removes momentum almost entirely — go lighter than your standing curl weight.
Squeeze hard at the top of each rep.

name: Triceps Pushdown
preparation: Stand facing a high pulley, gripping the bar or rope with elbows pinned at your sides.
execution: Push the attachment down until your arms are fully extended, then let it rise back under control.
formTips: Keep your elbows locked in place — only your forearms should move.
Avoid leaning your bodyweight into the movement to cheat the weight down.

name: Skull Crusher (Lying Triceps Extension)
preparation: Lie on a bench holding a barbell or dumbbells above your chest with arms extended.
execution: Lower the weight toward your forehead by bending only at the elbows, then extend back up.
formTips: Keep your upper arms stationary throughout — only your forearms should move.
Start light; this movement puts significant stress on the elbow joint.
commonMistakes: Letting the upper arms drift backward, which turns it into a pullover.
Using too much weight, which is a common cause of elbow strain on this exercise.
safetyNotes: Start light -- this movement puts significant, concentrated stress on the elbow joint.

name: Overhead Triceps Extension
preparation: Stand or sit holding a single dumbbell overhead with both hands.
execution: Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows, then extend back up.
formTips: Keep your elbows pointed forward, not flared out to the sides.
Brace your core to avoid arching your lower back.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
preparation: Lie on a bench and grip the bar at roughly shoulder width, closer than a standard bench press grip.
execution: Lower the bar to your lower chest keeping elbows tucked, then press back up.
formTips: This variation emphasizes the triceps more than a standard bench press.
Keep your elbows tucked close rather than flaring out.
commonMistakes: Gripping too narrow, which strains the wrists.
Flaring the elbows out instead of keeping them tucked.
safetyNotes: Use a spotter near your max the same as a standard bench press.

name: Bench Dip
preparation: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands gripping the edge beside your hips, legs extended in front of you.
execution: Lower your hips toward the floor by bending your elbows, then press back up.
formTips: Keep your shoulders down away from your ears throughout.
Bend your knees to make the movement easier if needed.

name: Plank
preparation: Rest on your forearms and toes, elbows under your shoulders, body in a straight line.
execution: Brace your core and hold the position without letting your hips sag or pike upward.
formTips: Squeeze your glutes to help keep your hips level.
Breathe steadily — don't hold your breath while bracing.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor as fatigue sets in.
Holding your breath instead of breathing steadily.

name: Side Plank
preparation: Lie on your side, resting on one forearm with your elbow under your shoulder and feet stacked.
execution: Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line, and hold without sagging.
formTips: Stack your hips directly on top of each other rather than rolling forward or back.
Add a top-arm reach overhead for an extra core challenge once the basic hold feels easy.

name: Crunch
preparation: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hands lightly supporting your head.
execution: Curl your shoulders off the floor toward your pelvis, then lower back down with control.
formTips: Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.
Exhale as you curl up to engage your abs more fully.

name: Bicycle Crunch
preparation: Lie on your back with hands lightly behind your head and knees pulled in toward your chest.
execution: Alternate bringing each elbow toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg out, in a pedaling motion.
formTips: Rotate through your torso rather than just moving your elbows.
Keep the motion slow and controlled rather than rushing through reps.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
preparation: Hang from a pull-up bar with arms fully extended.
execution: Raise your legs until roughly parallel to the floor (or higher) without swinging, then lower with control.
formTips: Bend your knees to make the movement easier while you build core strength.
Avoid using momentum from swinging your body.

name: Russian Twist
preparation: Sit with your knees bent and feet lifted slightly off the floor, torso leaned back a little.
execution: Rotate side to side, tapping the floor or a weight beside each hip.
formTips: Keep your chest up rather than rounding your back.
Move slower to increase difficulty instead of rushing through reps.

name: Cable Woodchopper
preparation: Set the pulley high and stand side-on to the machine, gripping the handle with both hands.
execution: Pull the handle diagonally down across your body to the opposite hip, rotating through your torso.
formTips: Let your hips and torso rotate together rather than just your arms pulling.
Keep your arms relatively straight — the power should come from your core.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
preparation: Kneel on the floor holding the ab wheel handles with both hands, wheel in front of you.
execution: Roll the wheel forward as far as you can control while keeping your core braced and back flat, then pull back to the start.
formTips: Only roll out as far as you can maintain a flat back — a sagging lower back means you've gone too far.
Start with partial-range rollouts before progressing to full extension.

name: Mountain Climber
preparation: Start in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders.
execution: Drive your knees alternately toward your chest at a quick pace, keeping your hips low.
formTips: Keep your core braced so your hips don't rise up as you pick up speed.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.

name: Dead Bug
preparation: Lie on your back with arms reaching straight up and knees bent at 90 degrees above your hips.
execution: Slowly extend one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor while keeping your lower back pressed down, then return and switch sides.
formTips: Keep your lower back flat against the floor the entire time — that's the whole point of the exercise.
Move slowly; this is a control exercise, not a speed one.

name: Jumping Jacks
preparation: Stand tall with feet together and arms at your sides.
execution: Jump your feet out wide while raising your arms overhead, then jump back to the starting position, repeating at a steady pace.
formTips: Land softly on the balls of your feet to reduce impact.
Keep a steady rhythm rather than rushing.

name: Burpee
preparation: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
execution: Drop into a squat, kick your feet back into a plank, do a push-up, jump your feet back in, then explode up into a jump.
formTips: Scale the push-up or jump to your fitness level while learning the pattern.
Keep your core braced during the plank phase to protect your lower back.

name: Jump Rope
preparation: Hold the rope handles at hip height, rope behind your heels.
execution: Turn the rope with your wrists and jump just high enough to clear it, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
formTips: Keep the jumps small and quick rather than high.
Turn the rope with your wrists, not your whole arms.

name: High Knees
preparation: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
execution: Jog in place, driving your knees up toward hip height as quickly as you can while pumping your arms.
formTips: Stay light on your feet rather than stomping down.
Keep your chest up and core engaged throughout.

name: Box Jump
preparation: Stand facing a sturdy box or platform in a quarter-squat position.
execution: Swing your arms and jump onto the box, landing softly with bent knees, then step back down.
formTips: Step down rather than jumping down to reduce impact on your joints.
Start with a lower box and increase height as your confidence grows.

name: Rowing Machine
preparation: Sit on the machine with feet strapped in and knees bent, gripping the handle with arms extended.
execution: Drive with your legs first, then lean back slightly and pull the handle to your ribs, reversing the sequence smoothly on the way forward.
formTips: The power sequence is legs, then back, then arms — reverse it on the way back.
Avoid rounding your lower back as you reach forward for the next stroke.

name: Battle Ropes
preparation: Stand in a stable athletic stance holding one rope end in each hand, arms extended toward the anchor point.
execution: Whip the ropes up and down alternately (or together) as fast as you can sustain for the interval.
formTips: Keep your knees slightly bent and core braced throughout.
Start with shorter intervals — this movement is more fatiguing than it looks.

name: Step-Up
preparation: Stand facing a sturdy bench or box, optionally holding a dumbbell in each hand.
execution: Step fully onto the bench with one foot, drive through that heel to stand tall, then step back down and repeat, alternating legs.
formTips: Push through your heel rather than pushing off your trailing foot.
Choose a step height that lets your knee stay behind your toes at the top.
